back: A router's list of destination networks, next hop and metric.
Static: routes set by hand. Dynamic: routers learn and update routes using a protocol.
Distance-vector; metric is hop count; whole table sent every 30 seconds; maximum 15 hops (16 is unreachable).
Link-state; metric is cost based on bandwidth; link-state database; shortest path with Dijkstra's idea; areas.
Cost = reference bandwidth ÷ link bandwidth, for example 100 ÷ bandwidth in Mbit/s; add the costs along a route.
RIP: simple, small networks, ignores speed. OSPF: large networks, uses link cost, fast adjusting, needs more router resources.
The number of routers a packet passes through; RIP's metric.
The map of links and costs held by every router in an OSPF area.
